output.summary: A flowering perennial native to Chiapas, Mexico, it naturally grows on other plants in wet forests and cloudy highland settings. Its deep forest-green, velvety, heart-shaped leaves have striking ivory to light-green veins, and it produces orange berries.
output.edibilityNote: Poisonous to humans when ingested; calcium oxalate crystals in the leaves can cause mouth and throat pain, nausea, swallowing difficulty and other symptoms.
